title: An animation studio that renders at night
summary: A Guadalajara studio renders a short film overnight on 200 VMs that read the same scenes. The artists work from their office and no scene can be lost.

requirements.1: {{s1}} holds the project folder, which the artists edit in place and hundreds of Linux servers mount at the same time over NFS, available in both zones.
requirements.2: {{s2}} keeps last night's version of the project folder, so a scene someone deletes by mistake can be recovered.
requirements.3: {{s3}} stores the finished frames for years; they are read over HTTP and survive the loss of an entire zone.
requirements.4: {{s4}} provides the render nodes: they can shut down with seconds or minutes of notice because the job resumes, and the lowest price with no commitment matters.
requirements.5: {{s5}} joins the office to the cloud network today, encrypted, over the internet it already has.
requirements.6: The artists work at the studio office in Guadalajara and upload their scenes from there.

s1.explanation: Azure Files provides NFS shares with a fully POSIX-compliant file system, on SSD with ZRS, and thousands of Linux clients use them at the same time. For in-place file editing, Microsoft recommends Azure Files, not NFS 3.0 on Blob Storage.
s1.hint_cue: mount at the same time over NFS

s2.explanation: A share snapshot is a read-only point-in-time copy, also for NFS, and lets you recover files one by one. Azure Backup does not support file shares that use the NFS protocol.

s3.explanation: With ZRS, Blob Storage copies the data synchronously across three or more zones and it stays available for reads and writes even if a zone fails. With LRS it stays in a single datacenter.
s3.hint_cue: survive the loss of an entire zone

s4.explanation: Azure evicts Spot VMs with 30 seconds of notice when it needs the capacity and they have no SLA, in exchange for significant savings. The render resumes on another VM.

s5.explanation: A VPN Gateway site-to-site connection builds an IPsec/IKE tunnel and sends encrypted traffic between the VNet and the office over the public internet.
s5.hint_cue: over the internet it already has

azure-managed-disks.s1: A managed disk is a block storage volume for VMs; sharing it across several VMs needs a cluster manager, and it is not an NFS share.
azure-managed-disks.s3: A managed disk is a block storage volume used with a VM; it does not serve the frames over HTTP.

azure-backup.s2: According to its support matrix, Azure Backup does not support file shares that use the NFS protocol, so it cannot back up this folder.

azure-blob-lrs.s3: LRS copies the data within a single datacenter, so the frames do not survive the loss of an entire zone.
azure-blob-lrs.s1: With LRS the data stays in a single datacenter, and Microsoft advises against NFS 3.0 on Blob Storage for in-place file editing.

azure-reservations.s4: A reservation lowers the price in exchange for committing to a one-year or three-year plan, and the requirement asks for the lowest price with no commitment.

azure-expressroute.s5: ExpressRoute extends the on-premises network to the cloud over a private connection through a connectivity provider and does not go over the public internet: it does not use the office's internet.

azure-blob-zrs.s1: Microsoft advises against NFS 3.0 on Blob Storage for general-purpose file shares and in-place file editing, because each edit rewrites the whole blob.
